intent: Hold the iteration 5 geometry exactly, so the Integrator can tune a controller on the best-evidenced platform and the final race uses a design with known behaviour. The only job for the Integrator is controller tuning on this fixed body. No geometry change is proposed for this final iteration.
learning: Iteration 5 is the reference. Across iterations 6 to 10, every single-variable change from it lowered the score, so further geometry tuning in the last iteration has negative expected value. If the Integrator reports that slalom line losses or s-bend off-track exits dominate, that points to controller line-loss handling and gain choice, not sensing, and the geometry should be left alone.
rationale: The best-supported design is still iteration 5 (score 422.9). Its layout is 5 sensors at y=0.07 m spanning x=±0.036 m with a 16 mm footprint, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg, and body 0.16 x 0.12 m. Every later single-variable test has scored lower or only matched it: mass 0.4 kg gave 422.1 with worse s-bend progress, track 0.09 m gave 347 with the oval finish falling to 60%, outer spread ±0.045 m gave 309, radius 0.045 m gave 390, and seven sensors at 12 mm pitch gave 331. Iteration 5 therefore remains the safest geometry to carry into the final unseen-track race. I keep it unchanged rather than add an untested variation, since the final race is scored once and cannot be repeated. The known weak points (s-bend off-track at max_error near 0.06 m, and slalom progress near 0.14 with about 1.85 line losses) are the controller's to address through gains and line-loss handling, and the Integrator can work on them without any geometry change. Expected result: about 420 to 425 on the development tracks, with oval finish near 95%.
